source.title: SOUL: Unlocking the Power of Second-Order Optimization for LLM Unlearning
source.authors: Jing-Han Jia; Yihua Zhang; Yimeng Zhang; Jiancheng Liu; Bharat Runwal; James Diffenderfer; B. Kailkhura; Si-Jia Liu

page_placements.theme: Membership-inference residue after unlearning (privacy signal, under- or over-unlearning)

record.tranche_reason: It evaluates unlearning outcomes and a jailbreak-prompt attack, but does not reproduce the proposed fine-tuning, activation-ablation, or quantization recovery tests.
record.gate_note: The paper measures forget-set accuracy before and after jailbreak prompting, alongside utility metrics. It does not test recovery by fine-tuning on a small set, activation-direction ablation, quantization, language changes, or ordinary prompt rephrasing. The reported membership-inference results concern training-data detectability, not recovery of targeted answers.
record.test_reason: The study proposes a new unlearning method (SOUL) and reports TOFU forget accuracy and utility for it and for first-order baselines. It also measures forget accuracy under Lynch et al.-style jailbreak prompts (Table A9). These results bear on A, E and F. B, C and D are not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that second-order optimization (SOUL) consistently beats first-order unlearning on efficacy while preserving utility across TOFU, copyright and detox tasks. They report a robustness advantage under non-optimized jailbreak prompts, while admitting that jailbreaking still degrades efficacy and that robustness was not comprehensively tested.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes SOUL, a second-order optimizer-based unlearning framework, and compares it with first-order unlearning methods; it does not test the recovery recipes in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Jailbreak prompts increase forget accuracy for the SO-GradDiff, SO-PO, and SO-NPO conditions. Outcomes also vary across unlearning objectives.

fits_no_version.finding: Min-k% MIA AUC on the forget set falls sharply for GradDiff/NPO variants (about 0.22–0.31), but stays near the original 0.79 for PO, FO-GA and input-based methods.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal-target unlearning (PO) leaves forgotten data detectable by membership inference, even when answer accuracy drops.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The paper does not specify a chance-level reference for forget accuracy. Its attack robustness evaluation is limited to the reported jailbreak prompts; the limitations section also says robustness was not comprehensively tested.
record.rows_left_out: The copyright-removal results in Table 4 and detoxification results in Table A7 are not extracted here; they report unlearning and utility comparisons, not recovery attacks, and the 48-row selection prioritizes the TOFU accuracy and jailbreak results. Other TOFU metrics (forget quality, Rouge-L, and MIA-related comparator detail beyond the recorded MIA values) are omitted.

untested.parts: No activation-direction ablation and no analysis of blocked access versus deletion.
Only one non-optimized jailbreak prompt type (a retain-set QA pair prefix). No rephrasing, other languages, other in-context information or optimized jailbreaks. Only tested on TOFU.
SOUL is tested only against that single jailbreak type. It is not tested against fine-tuning, ablation, quantization or optimized attacks, nor on copyright or detox tasks.
Robustness to attacks other than the single jailbreak is untested. No chance level is stated for TOFU forget accuracy.

missing.what: Influence unlearning (IU) baseline on TOFU: forget accuracy 84.25% versus original 85.25%, i.e. almost no forgetting.
Real-authors accuracy (a utility measure): e.g. SO-GradDiff 78%, FO-GA 42% and FO-GradDiff 71%, versus 89% originally.
Forget quality and forget Rouge-L on TOFU, which the authors use as primary efficacy measures.

record.verdict_notes: The jailbreak follows Lynch et al. (an original source), but this study is not itself an original source. Table A9 and Table 2 disagree on FO-GradDiff forget accuracy (72.25% vs 72.75%). There is no chance reference for TOFU accuracy; the metric picks the closest embedding among the ground truth and perturbed answers, so chance is likely around 15–20%. If so, the 10–16% values sit at or below chance, which is consistent with gibberish outputs.

versions.untested_parts: The paper reports forget accuracy and utility, but does not state a chance-level reference. It tests jailbreak robustness only for TOFU; the other recovery attacks in the claim are not tested.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning or relearning-set recovery attack.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis of access versus deletion.
Only jailbreak prompts are tested. No ordinary rephrasing, other languages, or in-context information.
SOUL is evaluated against the paper's jailbreak prompts only, not the other attack types named in the claim.

source_check.notes: Single non-optimized Lynch-style jailbreak (retain-set QA pair), TOFU LLaMA2-7B-chat only; no retrain or chance reference. Table A9 FO-GradDiff 72.25 vs Table 2 72.75. SOUL's 'robustness' is lower post-attack level; jailbreak gains are SO 5.75/2.5/4 vs FO 0/0/9.

statements.correction: Table 2, TOFU LLaMA2-7B-chat: forget acc FO-NPO 16.00%, SO-NPO 16.00% (original 85.25%); retain acc FO-NPO 80.75%, SO-NPO 81.25% (original 85.75%); world facts FO-NPO 82.91%, SO-NPO 85.47% (original 86.32%). No retrain model or chance level reported; comparison is to the original.
statements.problem: 'SO-NPO/FO-NPO ... retain 80.75/81.25%; world facts 82.91/85.47%' maps the pairs to the wrong methods: 80.75 and 82.91 are FO-NPO. The study also gives no retrain or gold reference for TOFU, only the original model.
72.25% for FO-GradDiff is the Table A9 value; Table 2 gives 72.75%.

statements.correction: Table A9: FO-GradDiff 72.25% before and after jailbreak (Table 2: 72.75%; original 85.25%), barely unlearned. FO-PO 37.00% before and after (original 85.25%); Table 2 FO-PO retain 82.75%, world facts 84.62%, so utility kept.
statements.problem: FO-PO is grouped with 'baselines that barely unlearned', but it dropped forget acc 85.25%->37.00% with utility kept; its unchanged 37.00% is a real no-recovery result, not little to recover. Only FO-GradDiff barely unlearned.

statements.correction: 2404.18239 (authors' own test): TOFU LLaMA2-7B-chat, one non-optimized Lynch-style jailbreak (retain-set QA pair). Forget acc after jailbreak: SO-GradDiff 16.00% vs FO-GradDiff 72.25%; SO-PO 31.25% vs FO-PO 37.00%; SO-NPO 20.00% vs FO-NPO 25.00% (Table A9). FO-GradDiff was 72.25% before the attack.
statements.problem: Cites r38, r40, r42 but says nothing about this study; its conditions (WMDP, harmful QA, personal info; GCG, AutoDAN, BDFinetune) exclude this study's TOFU setting and single retain-QA jailbreak. Direction of support matches verdict l5.

statements.correction: 2404.18239: TOFU LLaMA2-7B-chat, non-optimized Lynch-style jailbreak; SOUL forget acc rises SO-GradDiff 10.25->16.00%, SO-PO 28.75->31.25%, SO-NPO 16.00->20.00% (Table A9; original 85.25%). No retrain reference.
statements.problem: Cites r39, r40, r43, r44, r47, r48 but says nothing about this study; 'leakage stays above a retrained reference' does not apply, since the study has no retrain reference. Direction (partial loss of the effect) matches verdict l6.
